hero.statement: No changes were needed because the crab's energy thresholds were already written as fractions of ENERGY_MAX, so they stay correct now that ENERGY_MAX is 1.

My code already used ENERGY_MAX as a unit, so the change from 100 to 1 does not require any changes: HIDE_BELOW is still ENERGY_MAX * 0.3, spawn still sets energy: ENERGY_MAX, and all other numbers are movement or drawing values.
Updated the crab's hide threshold from 30 energy points to 0.3 because energy is now a fraction from 0 to 1.
My code already expresses the hide threshold as ENERGY_MAX * 0.3 and the hide/release logic uses ENERGY_MAX and HUNGRY_BELOW, so it works unchanged with the new energy-as-fraction rules.
My code still works because HIDE_BELOW is defined as ENERGY_MAX * 0.3, which now evaluates to 0.3 under the new fractional energy system, correctly representing 30%.
Updated DART_COST from 5 to 5/100 because ENERGY_MAX changed from 100 to 1, so the dart cost stays 5% of full energy.
Updated DART_ENERGY from 5 to ENERGY_MAX / 20 so it matches the new fractional energy model.
Updated DART_COST from a fixed 5 to ENERGY_MAX / 20 so the 5% cost stays correct now that ENERGY_MAX is 1.
The shared ENERGY_MAX changed from 100 to 1, so I updated the shrimp's DART_COST from 5 to 0.05 so each dart still spends the same fraction of full energy.
Since energy is now a fraction from 0 to 1, I changed DART_ENERGY from the hardcoded value 5 to ENERGY_MAX / 20, which is the same 5% of full energy expressed in the new unit.
